t: The chief seat of the Al Qasimi family on the Trucial Coast from the early nineteenth century.
It lived from pearling, fishing and trade, under British protection after the General Maritime Treaty of 1820.
Losing dependencies and trade to its neighbours, it joined the United Arab Emirates as a founding member in 1971.
dyk: Sharjah had the first airfield on the Trucial Coast: in 1932 Imperial Airways built a fortified rest house there, Al Mahatta, for passengers flying between Britain and India.
ev: Qawasim traditionally said to establish their rule at Sharjah
British expedition destroys Qasimi naval power; Sharjah becomes the family’s main seat
Sultan bin Saqr signs the General Maritime Treaty with Britain
Perpetual Maritime Truce ends warfare at sea
Exclusive Agreement places foreign relations under Britain
Imperial Airways opens a rest house and airfield at Sharjah
Britain deposes Sheikh Saqr bin Sultan
Sharjah joins the United Arab Emirates on 2 December
